page: The Vultr vhf-3c-8gb is an instance in the High Frequency Compute family. It features 3 shared vCPUs on an Intel x86_64 architecture operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz, coupled with 8.0 GB of system memory, which yields approximately 2.67 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware cache structures include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA, though AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent. Storage is provisioned locally as a 256 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one public IPv4 address without bundled hardware accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate mixed compute behavior across typical synthetic profiles. In basic compression benchmarks, single-threaded gzip performance lands in the top tier at 38.09 GB/sec, while single-core stress-ng (2401.69) and Geekbench single-core (1233.0) stay in the middle tier. However, multi-core metrics reveal shared-resource limits: Geekbench multi-core registers 2928.0, and PassMark overall CPU reaches 5738.4, both scoring in the lower tier. Memory access benchmarks exhibit strong small-block cached read throughput (395.59 GB/sec), yet uncached reads drop to 32.54 GB/sec and uncached writes fall to 16.94 GB/sec.

The instance delivers a balanced, entry-to-mid deployment profile by combining high-speed local NVMe storage with an atypical three-core layout. The primary tradeoff lies in the shared-core model and weak memory bandwidth under heavy uncached operational loads, such as large LLM inference or massive multi-core compilation. It functions effectively for web serving, microservices, continuous integration tasks, and lightweight operational databases where consistent single-threaded execution and direct NVMe response times are prioritized over multi-threaded throughput.
description: The Vultr vhf-3c-8gb is a High Frequency Compute instance delivering 3 shared Intel x86_64 vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz, 8.0 GB of RAM, and 256 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It includes one dedicated IPv4 address with no hardware accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place its single-core compute performance within the average tier, complemented by top-tier single-threaded gzip compression at 38.09 GB/sec. Due to its shared execution model and lower memory bandwidth on uncached transfers, multi-threaded workloads such as PassMark CPU tests and 7B LLM inference perform in lower percentiles. The server provides a cost-effective allocation of rapid local NVMe storage paired with moderate memory density, making it suitable for general web hosting, lightweight operational databases, and build environments.
